Q: I do not get powershell results in Windows 11 when queried through TCL exec A:

Found the root cause, and apparently not fixable via TCL script. The problem is in tclWinPipe.c;

Changing: createFlags = DETACHED_PROCESS;

to: createFlags = CREATE_NO_WINDOW;

This fixes the issue, but I am unsure on possible side-effects.

It seems that powershell depends on a console, else the code is not run. Bug report here: https://core.tcl-lang.org/tcl/tktview/cbbd2511ce

Q: Error: read ECONNRESET with Puppeteer and node 25.0.0 on windows A:

Yes, --single-process is the problem, and it's not just a Windows limitation — it's a flag that was never meant for production use with Puppeteer.

Why --single-process breaks things

Chrome normally runs as multiple processes: a browser process, GPU process, and one renderer process per tab. The --single-process flag forces everything into one process. This conflicts with how Puppeteer communicates with Chrome over the DevTools Protocol (CDP) via WebSocket.

What happens: Chrome launches, Puppeteer connects via WebSocket to ws://127.0.0.1:PORT/devtools/browser/..., but the single-process mode makes Chrome unstable — the browser process crashes or resets the connection before Puppeteer finishes the handshake. That's your ECONNRESET.

Node 25 made this more visible because it ships with a newer version of the ws library that handles connection errors differently (it surfaces them instead of silently swallowing them).

The fix

Remove --single-process and --no-zygote from your args:

var puppeteer_options = {
    headless: true,
    ignoreHTTPSErrors: true,
    args: [
        '--no-sandbox',
        '--disable-setuid-sandbox',
        '--disable-dev-shm-usage',
        '--shm-size=4gb',
    ],
    defaultViewport: { width: 1920, height: 1080 },
    protocolTimeout: 1000000,
};

--no-zygote is typically paired with --single-process and can also cause stability issues on Windows. Drop both.

If you were using --single-process for memory reasons

The usual reason people add this flag is to reduce memory in constrained environments (Docker, cheap VPS). Better alternatives:

  • Use headless: 'shell' (Puppeteer 21+) — runs Chrome's headless shell which uses significantly less memory than full headless Chrome
  • Limit pages: close tabs you're done with via await page.close()
  • Use --disable-gpu and --disable-extensions to trim memory further
args: [
    '--no-sandbox',
    '--disable-setuid-sandbox',
    '--disable-dev-shm-usage',
    '--disable-gpu',
    '--disable-extensions',
],
headless: 'shell',

This gives you low memory usage without the instability of --single-process.

Q: Set cell to data validation any value if condition is true, if not set data validation to list. VBA or formula A:

There are two ways to handle this.
You can get pretty close to what you want using only dynamic named range. Create new named range (Formulas=>Name Manager) and referes to a conditional formula : "If(Sheet1!$A$1=TRUE,Sheet1!$A$10,Sheet1!$G$1:$G$10)"
(replace Sheet1 with the name of your sheet. )
The select C1, in data validation choose "List" as the type and in the source field write the name of the named range.
This works, but here's the catch: it's not 100% automatic. What this actually does is change the content of the dropdown list depending on A1 — so if A1 is TRUE, the dropdown will only offer "MyRoute" as a choice, and if A1 is FALSE, it'll offer your DifferentPlaces list. But C1 itself won't auto-fill or auto-update on its own — you (or whoever's using the sheet) still has to click the dropdown and pick a value manually.

If you really need C1 to update itself the instant A1 changes, with zero clicks involved, VBA is the way to go.
For that, you need to used the Worksheet_Change event.
In the sheet module :

Private Sub Worksheet_Change(ByVal Target As Range)
    If Not Intersect(Target, Me.Range("A1")) Is Nothing Then
        UpdateC1
    End If
End Sub

Private Sub UpdateC1()
    Application.EnableEvents = False
    On Error Resume Next
    Me.Range("C1").Validation.Delete

    If Me.Range("A1").Value = True Then
        Me.Range("C1").Value = Me.Range("A10").Value
    Else
        Me.Range("C1").ClearContents
        With Me.Range("C1").Validation
            .Add Type:=xlValidateList, AlertStyle:=xlValidAlertStop, _
                 Operator:=xlBetween, Formula1:="=$G$1:$G$10"
            .IgnoreBlank = True
            .InCellDropdown = True
        End With
    End If

    On Error GoTo 0
    Application.EnableEvents = True
End Sub

Hope that helps :)
